views.description: Circular shaft end profile with an axial keyway at the right-hand perimeter. The concentric dashed circle represents the reduced-diameter neck behind the end collar, not a bore.

views.description: Longitudinal side view with a conventional central break, end collars, two reduced-diameter circumferential necks, and longitudinal keyway edges. The partial end view at the left repeats the separately supplied front view and is not an additional independent view.
views.centerline_notes: Longitudinal centerline identifies a common shaft axis through the body, collars, and reduced necks. The break shortens the drawn length only; it is not a physical separation.

features.description: Base shaft: circular front-plane profile of nominal reference diameter 2.4985, extruded axially 76.88. Retain the large diameter for the central body and end collars.

Axial external keyway at the right of the front profile, width .500 +.002/-.000 centered on the horizontal diameter; floor 2.218 from the opposite outside tangent. Longitudinal edges indicate a full-length axial cut, interrupted naturally by the reduced necks.

Left circumferential neck, reducing the shaft to diameter 1.734 over axial width 1.016. Measured from the left end, the neck runs from .880 to 1.896. The collar-side shoulder at .880 is datum B. This is annular removal, not a one-sided rectangular pocket.

Right circumferential neck, diameter 1.734 and axial width 1.016. From the left end, its collar-side shoulder is at .880 + 75.125 = 76.005, and its body-side shoulder is at 74.989. Remaining right collar width is .875. This is annular removal.
Typical concave root radii at both neck shoulders, four circular root edges in total; radius must not exceed .125. Exact selected radius is unspecified.
Provisional .06 corner-radius treatment at the outside edges of both shaft ends. Confirm the meaning of C/R before implementing this as a fillet rather than an allowed chamfer/radius treatment.

symmetry.plane: Longitudinal plane through shaft axis and horizontal diameter of front view
symmetry.description: CENT places the two keyway walls equally above and below this plane.

concentric_groups.description: Main outside diameter, both end collars, and both reduced-diameter necks share the longitudinal shaft axis.

dimension_chains.description: Overall length = left collar + inner-shoulder span + derived right collar: .880 + 75.125 + .875 = 76.880.
Inner-shoulder span = left neck + central body + right neck: 1.016 + 73.093 + 1.016 = 75.125; repeated D005 denotes the two TYP instances.
Nominal reference outside diameter = opposite-tangent-to-keyway-floor distance + derived radial keyway depth: 2.218 + .2805 = 2.4985.

warnings: No title block is supplied: part identification, revision, scale, explicit drawing standard, material grade, and general tolerances cannot be established.
Inches are inferred from the dimension conventions and shaft callouts; an explicit units declaration is absent.

Datum A identifier is visible beside the front-view keyway dimensions, but its exact feature attachment is not unambiguous. Do not assume it is the shaft axis without confirmation. Datum B is the left collar inner shoulder.
The .06 C/R BOTH ENDS numerical callout is clear, but its abbreviation requires confirmation; corner radius is the provisional interpretation.
The .125 R MAX TYP callout does not specify a unique fillet radius. The feature describes four matching root transitions, but the chosen radius must respect the maximum.

If equal .88-wide end collars were intended, 75.125 + 2(.88) would equal 76.885, differing from the printed overall length by .005. Extraction instead preserves the printed values and derives a .875 right collar; exact axial mirror symmetry is not established.
The stock diameter is expressly REF, despite its printed ±.0015 range. Derived keyway radial coordinates are therefore nominal and must not replace the controlling 2.218 dimension.
Keyway full axial extent is inferred from the longitudinal edges; no separate axial keyway length or termination dimension is printed.
MACHINE CENTERS PERMITTED is an allowance for optional manufacturing centers, not a dimensioned center-hole requirement; no holes have been invented.
CFS likely denotes cold-finished steel; the associated H surface marking has no supplied legend.

The neck features use the available extrude_cut category to describe annular material removal. Their dimensional source is the side view; a CAD implementation must use an annular axial cut or a revolved cut, not blindly extrude a side-view rectangle.
